USA.note: USDA PSD 2024/25: prod 377.6 / cons (domestic, incl. ~140 Mt feed + ~140 Mt ethanol/FSI) 318.3 / exp 72.5 / imp 1.9 Mt. US corn exports were a record ~72.5 Mt MY2024/25 (USDA/U.S. Grains Council).

CHN.note: USDA PSD 2024/25: prod ~294.9 / cons ~313 / imp ~8 Mt. Imports fell sharply from ~23 Mt in 2023/24 as Beijing curbed inbound corn to protect domestic prices.

BRA.note: USDA PSD 2024/25 (local Mar-Feb MY): prod ~127 / cons ~87 / exp ~40 Mt (ITC calendar-2024 shipments 39.8 Mt). Most output is the safrinha second crop after soybeans.

EU.note: USDA/EU customs 2024/25: prod ~59 / cons ~78 / imports ~19.5 Mt (Spain, Netherlands, Italy, Portugal, Ireland the largest buyers); exports ~3 Mt. EU is a structural net maize importer for feed.

ARG.note: USDA PSD 2024/25: prod ~51 / cons ~14 / exp ~36 Mt (ITC calendar-2024 32.1 Mt; spider/leafhopper 'chicharrita' damage cut early-2024 output). Argentina is the #3-4 global exporter.

MEX.note: USDA PSD 2024/25: prod ~23.5 / cons ~48.5 / imp ~25 Mt (largest single maize importer; ~99% from the US). Mostly yellow feed corn; domestic crop is mainly white corn for food.

UKR.note: USDA 2024/25: prod ~26.5 / exp ~22 Mt (ITC calendar-2024 29.6 Mt reflects 2023/24 carryover shipments). Drought trimmed the 2024 crop; the EU absorbs ~half of exports as China demand fell.

IND.note: USDA PSD 2024/25: prod ~37.7 Mt. Surging domestic feed + ethanol demand turned India from a steady exporter into a marginal net importer for the first time in years.

JPN.note: USDA PSD 2024/25: imports ~15.5 Mt, almost entirely feed and FSI corn. Japan grows essentially no field corn; the US supplies the large majority, with Brazil/Argentina second.

VNM.note: USDA PSD 2024/25: imp ~12 Mt for a fast-growing feed sector (pork/poultry/aquaculture). South America (Brazil, Argentina) dominates supply; US share rose sharply in 2024/25.

KOR.note: USDA PSD 2024/25: imp ~11.5 Mt (feed + starch). Korea buys flexibly from Brazil, Argentina, the US and the Black Sea, switching origins on price.

EGY.note: USDA PSD 2024/25: imp ~8.5 Mt for poultry/livestock feed. FX scarcity squeezed volumes; Brazil became the leading supplier in 2024, with Ukraine and Argentina also key.

IRN.note: USDA PSD 2024/25: imp ~7 Mt for feed; sanctions and FX shortages make volumes volatile. Brazil and Russia are leading suppliers; calendar-2024 import value fell ~70% y/y.

COL.note: USDA PSD 2024/25: imp ~6.7 Mt, almost entirely US yellow corn for feed (poultry/pork). Colombia is consistently a top-5 destination for US corn.

TWN.note: USDA PSD 2024/25: imp ~4.5 Mt feed corn, sourced mainly from the US and Brazil/Argentina on price.

DZA.note: USDA PSD 2024/25: imp ~4.5 Mt. Algeria runs a state-tendered feed-corn import program; Argentina, Brazil and the Black Sea compete for the business.

SAU.note: USDA PSD 2024/25: imp ~4.3 Mt feed corn for its large poultry/dairy sector; Argentina, Brazil and Ukraine are leading suppliers.

MYS.note: USDA PSD 2024/25: imp ~4.2 Mt feed corn; Argentina and Brazil dominate supply to SE Asia.

DEU.note: ITC/Comtrade 2024: Germany is a net maize importer (~US$0.95bn imports vs ~US$0.18bn exports); intra-EU plus Ukraine/Black Sea supply. Figures are indicative kt within the EU-27 bloc.

ESP.note: USDA/EU customs 2024/25: Spain is the EU's largest maize importer (~8-9 Mt) for feed; Brazil, Ukraine, the US and Argentina supply the Mediterranean.

ITA.note: USDA/EU customs 2024/25: Italy imports ~5-6 Mt despite domestic output ~6 Mt; strong feed and food (polenta/starch) demand. Ukraine and Brazil are leading suppliers.

NLD.note: ITC/Comtrade 2024: the Netherlands imports ~US$1.28bn of maize and re-exports a large share via Rotterdam (a major EU grain gateway). Net position near balance; figures indicative kt.

MAR.note: USDA PSD 2024/25: Morocco imports ~3 Mt feed corn; Brazil, Argentina and the Black Sea compete for the trade.

PER.note: USDA PSD 2024/25: Peru imports ~3.7 Mt yellow corn for its large poultry sector; the US and Argentina/Brazil supply the Pacific coast.

TUR.note: USDA PSD 2024/25: Turkey produces ~8.5 Mt but still imports ~4 Mt for feed; Ukraine and Russia (Black Sea) are natural suppliers. 2024 import value jumped ~72% y/y.

CAN.note: USDA PSD 2024/25: prod ~15.5 Mt; near-balanced trade (exports to the US/EU; imports of US corn into eastern Canada). Roughly net neutral.

RUS.note: USDA PSD 2024/25: prod ~13.5 / exp ~3.5 Mt. Drought cut the 2024 crop and exports sharply (ITC value down ~56% y/y); Turkey, Iran and the Caucasus are key markets.

ZAF.note: USDA PSD 2024/25: prod ~13 / exp ~2.8 Mt. South Africa is sub-Saharan Africa's swing supplier; a 2024 drought cut the white-maize crop and lifted regional prices.

ZWE.note: USDA PSD 2024/25: El Nino drought devastated the 2024 maize crop, forcing large imports (mostly white maize from South Africa/Zambia/overseas). Import value up >200% y/y.

GTM.note: USDA PSD 2024/25: Guatemala imports ~1.4 Mt, overwhelmingly US yellow corn for feed under CAFTA-DR.

IDN.note: USDA PSD 2024/25: Indonesia produces ~11.5 Mt and limits feed-corn imports via policy; residual imports ~1 Mt+ in deficit years from Argentina/Brazil.

PRY.note: USDA PSD 2024/25: prod ~5.3 / exp ~3.8 Mt. Paraguay is a consistent South American exporter shipping via the Parana-Paraguay river system to Brazil and overseas.

FRA.note: ITC/Comtrade 2024: France is the EU's largest maize exporter (~US$1.86bn, ~4 Mt), shipping within the EU and to North Africa. A wet 2024 trimmed the crop.

ROU.note: ITC/Comtrade 2024: Romania exported ~US$0.89bn (~2.9 Mt) of maize via Constanta, serving as both a producer and a Black Sea transit hub for Ukrainian grain.

HUN.note: ITC/Comtrade 2024: Hungary exported ~US$0.87bn (~2.4 Mt), supplying the EU feed market and the Adriatic/Mediterranean.

SRB.note: ITC/Comtrade 2024: Serbia exported ~US$0.46bn (+66% y/y) of maize, mainly to the EU and the Balkans/Mediterranean.

MMR.note: ITC/Comtrade 2024: Myanmar exported ~US$0.69bn (+53% y/y) of maize, almost entirely overland/by sea to Thailand and China for feed.

flows.note: Mexico is the #1 destination for US corn: ~24-25 Mt in MY2024/25, ~99% of Mexico's ~25 Mt imports (USDA/U.S. Grains Council). ITC: US$5.2bn of US corn to Mexico in 2024.
ITC 2024: US supplied US$3.0bn (+30% y/y) of Japan's corn, ~75% of Japan's ~15.5 Mt imports; ~11 Mt. The US is Japan's dominant supplier.
Colombia took ~6-7 Mt of US corn in 2024 (USDA/U.S. Grains Council), nearly all of its ~6.7 Mt imports; a consistent top-5 US market.
ITC 2024: US corn to South Korea US$0.64bn (+118% y/y), ~3 Mt, as Korea shifted toward US origin on competitive Gulf/PNW pricing.
Taiwan is a steady US corn market (~3 Mt in 2024/25), buying feed corn under long-running purchasing missions (U.S. Grains Council).
US corn to Vietnam jumped from ~5 kt in 2023/24 to ~1.1 Mt in 2024/25, putting Vietnam in the US top-10 for the first time (USDA/U.S. Grains Council).
Modeled: the US supplies the bulk of Peru's ~3.7 Mt yellow-corn imports for poultry (USDA PSD gap + U.S. Grains Council market share). Argentina/Brazil take the balance.
Modeled: Guatemala's ~1.4 Mt imports are overwhelmingly US yellow corn under CAFTA-DR (USDA PSD gap; US is the near-exclusive supplier to Central America).
ITC 2024: US corn to China US$0.56bn (-78% y/y) as Beijing slashed imports; ~2 Mt, down from ~7 Mt the prior year. US was China's #3 supplier behind Brazil and Ukraine.
USDA 2024/25: the US gained EU market share on abundant supply, shipping ~3-4 Mt into Spain/Portugal/Italy as a swing supplier alongside Ukraine and Brazil.
Modeled: the US competes for Algeria's ~4.5 Mt feed-corn tenders against South America and the Black Sea; share varies by freight (USDA PSD; US a periodic supplier).
Modeled: the US is a secondary supplier to Saudi Arabia's ~4.3 Mt feed-corn market behind Argentina/Brazil/Ukraine (USDA PSD gap).
Modeled: the US ships periodically into Morocco's ~3 Mt feed-corn market when freight is competitive vs South America/Black Sea (USDA PSD gap).
ITC 2024: Brazil was China's #1 corn supplier at US$1.9bn (-53% y/y as China cut total imports); ~5-6 Mt. Brazil overtook the US as China's top corn origin in 2023-24.
Brazil was Egypt's leading supplier in 2024: ~3.5 Mt Jan-Oct (+240% y/y), ~14% of Brazil's exports (ANEC/SECEX). Egypt was Brazil's #1 corn destination in 2024.
Vietnam took ~3.3 Mt of Brazilian corn Jan-Oct 2024 (ANEC/SECEX), one of Brazil's largest markets as SE Asian feed demand grew.
Iran imported ~2.7 Mt of Brazilian corn Jan-Oct 2024 (ANEC/SECEX); Brazil is a leading supplier to Iran's feed sector despite FX constraints.
ITC 2024: Brazil was South Korea's #1 corn supplier at US$0.82bn; ~2.6 Mt (ANEC/SECEX Jan-Oct). Korea buys Brazilian/Argentine origin flexibly.
ITC 2024: Brazil supplied US$0.80bn (-62% y/y) of Japan's corn, ~2.4 Mt; Japan's #2 origin after the US, switching on price.
Modeled: Brazil competes for Algeria's ~4.5 Mt feed-corn tenders alongside Argentina and the Black Sea (ANEC/SECEX shows North Africa among growing Brazilian markets).
Modeled: Brazil and Argentina are leading suppliers to Saudi Arabia's ~4.3 Mt feed-corn market (ANEC/SECEX; USDA PSD gap).
Modeled: Brazil and Argentina dominate supply to Malaysia's ~4.2 Mt feed-corn market (USDA PSD gap; ANEC SE-Asia flows).
ITC 2024: Brazil supplied US$0.27bn (+54% y/y) of Mexico's corn (~1 Mt), Mexico's #2 origin as it began diversifying beyond the US.
Modeled: Brazil is a major supplier to Spain and the EU Mediterranean for feed corn alongside Ukraine and Argentina (USDA/EU customs flows).
Modeled: Argentina is a top supplier to Vietnam's ~12 Mt feed-corn market; South America (ARG+BRA) covers the large majority (USDA PSD gap; ITC SE-Asia flows).
ITC 2024: Argentina supplied US$0.74bn of South Korea's corn (~2.7 Mt), Korea's #2 origin after Brazil.
Modeled: Argentina is historically a leading winner of Algeria's feed-corn tenders (~4.5 Mt market); competitive Up-River freight to the Mediterranean (USDA PSD gap).
Modeled: Argentina is a leading supplier to Saudi Arabia's ~4.3 Mt feed-corn market (USDA PSD gap; long-standing Gulf trade).
Modeled: Argentina and Brazil dominate supply to Malaysia's ~4.2 Mt feed market (USDA PSD gap; ITC SE-Asia flows).
Modeled: Argentina (and Brazil) supply the non-US share of Peru's ~3.7 Mt yellow-corn imports for poultry (USDA PSD gap).
Modeled: Argentina is a recurring supplier to Egypt's ~8.5 Mt feed-corn market alongside Brazil and Ukraine (USDA PSD gap).
Modeled: Argentina supplies the EU Mediterranean (Spain/Italy) for feed corn alongside Brazil and Ukraine (USDA/EU customs flows).
USDA/EU customs 2024/25: the EU is Ukraine's principal corn destination, taking roughly half of its ~22 Mt exports (Spain, Italy, Netherlands, Portugal the main buyers).
ITC 2024: Ukraine was China's #2 corn supplier at US$1.1bn (-37% y/y); ~5 Mt. Chinese demand for Ukrainian corn fell sharply as Beijing cut total imports.
Egypt bought ~1.6 Mt of Ukrainian corn in 2024/25 despite FX stress (IGC/Argus); down from ~3.6 Mt in 2023/24 as Brazil gained share.
Turkey lifted purchases of Ukrainian corn in 2024/25 (IGC/Argus), partly filling the gap left by reduced Russian exports; ~2-3 Mt.
Spain is a major buyer of Ukrainian corn within the EU; ~2 Mt in Oct-Dec 2024 alone vs 5.5 Mt for full 2023/24 (IGC/Argus), reflecting slower early-season pace.
Modeled: Turkey and Iran are the natural Black Sea markets for Russia's ~3.5 Mt corn exports; 2024 drought cut Russian volumes sharply (USDA PSD; ITC value -56% y/y).
Modeled: Russia is a leading supplier to Iran's ~7 Mt feed-corn market alongside Brazil (USDA PSD gap; Caspian/Black Sea logistics).
Modeled: South Africa supplies white maize to drought-hit Zimbabwe and the SADC region; the 2024 El Nino drought hit both, tightening regional balances (USDA PSD).
ITC 2024: South Africa shipped yellow maize to East Asia (Korea/Japan) when surplus; volumes fell sharply (-97% to Korea) after the 2024 drought.
Modeled: France, the EU's largest maize exporter (~4 Mt), ships mostly intra-EU (Benelux, Iberia) plus some to North Africa (ITC/Comtrade 2024).
Modeled: Romania exports ~2.9 Mt via Constanta, much of it intra-EU plus transit of Ukrainian grain to Mediterranean and MENA markets (ITC/Comtrade 2024).
Modeled: Hungary's ~2.4 Mt of exports go mostly to neighbouring EU/Adriatic markets for feed (ITC/Comtrade 2024).
Modeled: Myanmar's ~2.8 Mt corn exports go largely overland to Thailand (border feed trade) and to China (ITC/Comtrade 2024; +53% y/y growth).
ITC 2024: Myanmar supplied US$54m of China's corn (China's #4 origin), reflecting cross-border feed trade into Yunnan.
Modeled: Paraguay ships much of its ~3.8 Mt exports to/through Brazil and Argentina via the Parana-Paraguay river system, plus direct overseas sales (USDA PSD).
ITC 2024: Paraguay supplied US$0.08bn of South Korea's corn (~0.3 Mt), a niche but recurring Mercosur origin for Asian buyers.
Modeled: Brazil and Argentina supply the non-US share of Taiwan's ~4.5 Mt feed-corn imports (USDA PSD gap; ITC East-Asia flows).
Modeled: Argentina is a secondary supplier to Taiwan's feed-corn market behind the US and Brazil (USDA PSD gap).

rankings.note: Exporter/importer bar values are kt for marketing year 2024/25 from USDA PSD/Grain (corn). Note: USDA marketing-year tonnages differ modestly from ITC Trade Map calendar-2024 shipments (e.g. ITC has US 62.6 / Brazil 39.8 / Argentina 32.1 / Ukraine 29.6 Mt for CY2024). EU shown as the EU-27 import bloc (~19.5 Mt); France/Romania/Hungary are large intra-/extra-EU exporters within it.

companies.name: Cargill
companies.metric: Group revenue ≈US$160bn (FY2024); operates in ~70 countries; one of the 'ABCD' grain majors.
companies.note: World's largest privately held company and a top global grain/oilseed trader; major corn origination and export elevation in the US Gulf, Brazil and the Black Sea.
companies.improve: As a private company under no SEC-filing pressure, Cargill discloses little segment-level corn volume or origin data. It should publish corn-specific origination by country and freight-route, plus traceability for Cerrado-origin feed grain, so customers and regulators can size land-use and concentration risk.

companies.name: Archer-Daniels-Midland (ADM)
companies.metric: Revenue ≈US$85bn (FY2024); Ag Services & Oilseeds is its largest segment; major US corn processor (wet milling, ethanol, sweeteners).
companies.note: Leading US corn processor and global merchandiser; large ethanol, starch and sweetener operations consume domestic corn, plus an international grain trading book.
companies.improve: ADM's corn footprint spans origination, processing and ethanol, but its disclosures blend corn into 'Ag Services'. Breaking out corn origination volume by country and the deforestation/land-use exposure of its South American sourcing would let the market price feedstock and policy risk.

companies.name: Bunge Global (Bunge-Viterra)
companies.metric: Revenue ≈US$53bn (FY2024); 2024-25 merger with Viterra creates a top-tier global grain/oilseed handler.
companies.note: A core 'ABCD' trader with deep South American (Brazil/Argentina) origination; the Viterra combination adds Black Sea, Canadian and Australian reach in corn and other grains.
companies.improve: Post-Viterra, Bunge becomes one of the largest corn handlers in the Americas and Black Sea. It should publish combined corn origination by country and concentration metrics, and detail how the enlarged network manages Mercosur land-use and Black Sea war-risk exposure.

companies.name: Louis Dreyfus Company (LDC)
companies.metric: Net sales ≈US$50bn (FY2024); the 'D' of the ABCD majors; significant grains & oilseeds platform.
companies.note: Global merchandiser with strong Latin American and Black Sea corn origination and a large port/logistics network.
companies.improve: LDC is privately held and discloses little corn-specific volume. Publishing origin-level corn handled and traceability for South American grain would improve transparency on land-use and counterparty concentration, where it lags listed peers.

companies.name: COFCO International
companies.metric: China's largest food/agri group's global trading arm; multi-billion-tonne grain & oilseed volumes; key channel for China's corn imports.
companies.note: The overseas trading platform of state-owned COFCO; a primary conduit for Brazilian, Argentine, Ukrainian and US corn into China and a growing third-party trader.
companies.improve: As a state-linked buyer central to China's food security, COFCO's disclosure is limited. Publishing corn import volumes by origin and storage/inventory positions would help the market read Chinese demand swings that move global corn prices.

companies.name: Viterra
companies.metric: Large global grain handler with extensive Canadian, Australian, Argentine and Black Sea networks; combining with Bunge in 2024-25.
companies.note: Strong corn origination in Argentina and the Black Sea plus North American grain assets; the Bunge merger reshapes the competitive map.
companies.improve: Through the Bunge combination, Viterra's corn assets concentrate further. Clear pre/post-merger disclosure of corn origination by country and of how overlapping Argentine/Black Sea positions are managed would address concentration and antitrust scrutiny.

global.note: World maize production/consumption/exports in kt by marketing year, USDA PSD/Grain. Global output and trade hit record highs in 2024/25 (consumption ~1.24-1.32 Bt; trade ~199 Mt per ITC CY2024). Series rounded; 2024 = MY2024/25 estimate.

forecast.method: Projected 2030 value = 2024 value × (1 + CAGR)^6, per metric. Net = projected production − projected consumption. CAGRs are reasoned assumptions inside the OECD-FAO Agricultural Outlook 2024-2033 and USDA envelopes (global coarse-grain/maize demand rising ~1.0-1.3%/yr, driven by feed in Asia and ethanol), stated openly so they can be challenged.

scenarios.label: US Corn Belt drought cuts exports 20%
scenarios.note: The US supplies ~30% of world corn exports (~72 Mt); a Midwest drought like 2012 can cut the crop ~15-25% and sharply tighten exportable supply, hitting Mexico, Japan, Colombia and Korea hardest.

scenarios.label: Brazil safrinha failure cuts exports 30%
scenarios.note: Over 75% of Brazil's crop is the weather-exposed safrinha second corn; a dry/hot window (as in 2021) can slash output and the ~40 Mt export program, raising prices for China, Egypt, Vietnam and Iran.

scenarios.label: Ukraine Black Sea corridor disruption -50%
scenarios.note: Ukraine exports ~22 Mt of corn, roughly half to the EU; renewed Black Sea blockade or escalation could halve flows, as in 2022. The EU, China, Egypt and Turkey would scramble for substitutes.

scenarios.label: Argentina raises corn export taxes/curbs -40%
scenarios.note: Argentina has repeatedly used export taxes (retenciones) and registration limits on grains; a tightening would pull ~14 Mt off the world market, lifting prices for SE Asia, Algeria, Saudi Arabia and Peru.

scenarios.label: China corn import surge (herd rebuild) +15 Mt
scenarios.note: China's corn imports swing widely (from ~23 Mt in 2023/24 to ~8 Mt in 2024/25). A hog-herd rebuild or poor domestic harvest could add 10-15 Mt of import demand, tightening Brazilian, Ukrainian and US balances.

scenarios.label: Southern Africa El Nino drought (regional deficit)
scenarios.note: El Nino droughts (as in 2024) cut South Africa's ~13 Mt crop and devastate Zimbabwe/Zambia/Malawi white-maize harvests, forcing large emergency imports and spiking regional food prices.
